lede: CPI at 8:30 AM; banks profit but warn on rates; ASML says demand exceeds supply; oil firmer on Iran shipping tactics.
geo_headlines: CPI AT 8:30 AM IS THE EVENT. September CPI is expected to rise to 3.7% a year from 3.4% in August, with core at 2.5% from 2.4% (Investopedia); prediction-market traders price 3.6% (CNBC). **New York Fed President Williams said overnight he still sees one more hike this year but downplayed the need for another in 2027 (Reuters).** FedWatch, as of Tuesday 10/13: October hike 22.1%, December 89.4%.

BANKS: STRONG PROFITS, STOCKS DOWN. Goldman earned $17.01 a share vs $13.02 expected and Citi $2.85 vs $2.66; JPMorgan missed at $5.57 vs $5.90, and Wells Fargo's revenue missed (CNBC). All four closed lower, Citi down about 5.5% (Investopedia). Dimon warned that a move in rates from 5% to 6% would hurt more than 4% to 5%, adding he is not predicting it (CNBC).

ASML BEAT; CHIPS STEADIER. ASML posted Q3 sales of 11.7 billion euros and said planned supply for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet demand, with some customers asking about 2029-2030 orders (ASML). In Asia, Samsung rose 2.8% and SK Hynix 2.0% early as the chip selloff eased (Investing.com); the Kospi closed down 0.4% at 6,008.81 (AP). China's September exports rose 36.3% vs 25.5% expected.

OIL FIRMER ON NEW IRAN TACTICS. Brent December $106.56 (+0.8%), WTI November $95.63 (+1.6%). Iranian officials told Reuters Tehran has shifted tactics to step up attacks on ships and keep oil high before the US midterms, and will expand beyond Hormuz to the Gulf of Oman (Reuters). Iran said a cargo ship carrying 2,500 containers sank after hitting a mine Wednesday; not independently verified (AP).

FUTURES A TOUCH HIGHER. S&P 500 futures 7,868.25 (+0.16%), Nasdaq 100 futures 30,757.75 (-0.11%) as of 6:55 AM ET. Tuesday: S&P 500 7,805.45 (-0.02%), 0.17% below its October 6 record close; Nasdaq 100 -0.31%; Dow -0.35%. The 10-year yield fell 3 basis points to 5.21%. VIX 15.27.

TODAY: BANK OF AMERICA, MORGAN STANLEY, BEIGE BOOK. Bank of America call 8:30 AM; Morgan Stanley results about 7:30 AM, call 9:30 AM; BlackRock before the open (company releases). Fed Beige Book 2:00 PM. Thursday: retail sales, PPI, TSMC. Friday: options expiration.
client_frame_short: Today is about inflation. September's consumer price report at 8:30 is expected to show prices up about 3.7% from a year ago, mostly because of energy, with core inflation near 2.5%. **The banks told the more useful story yesterday: profits are strong, but rates near 5% are starting to bite, and Jamie Dimon warned that a move to 6% would hurt more than the move to 5% did.** Stocks are steady, 0.17% below their record. For clients: a hot headline number is mostly energy, and the long-term plan does not change.
client_frame:
If a client calls this morning, the story is the inflation report, read through what the banks said yesterday.

The report: at 8:30 AM the government publishes September consumer prices. Forecasters expect 3.7% over the past year, up from 3.4%, driven mainly by gasoline and energy. Core inflation, which strips out food and energy, is expected around 2.5%. That gap is the point: most of the increase is oil, not a broad wage-price spiral.

The banks: the four biggest reporters showed strong profits, led by Goldman, which earned $17.01 a share against $13.02 expected. Even so, all four stocks fell, because management warned that higher rates and sticky inflation are starting to bite. Jamie Dimon said a move in rates from 5% to 6% would be more painful than the move from 4% to 5%, while saying clearly he is not predicting it.

The Fed: New York Fed President Williams still sees one more hike this year but not more in 2027. Futures put an October hike near 22%.

Oil: Brent is about $106. Iranian officials told Reuters they are stepping up attacks on shipping to keep prices high before the US midterm elections. That is the inflation story in one sentence.

Chips: ASML, the maker of the machines that make advanced chips, said it cannot fully meet demand through 2028, a useful counterweight to this week's AI funding scare.

Why it matters: higher-for-longer rates are good news for savers and bond buyers and a headwind for borrowers and richly valued stocks. Diversified portfolios are built for this mix.

For clients, the message holds: high-quality bonds pay more than 5% for a decade, and long-term equity plans do not need changing. What would change the view: a 10-year close above 5.40% (Tuesday 5.21%), a 30-year above 5.75% (Tuesday 5.56%), or US strikes on Iran that keep Brent well above $105 (now $106.56).
